newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Chechen separatist leader leaves for Moscow talks.
newsitem.headline: Chechen separatist leader leaves for Moscow talks.

text.p: Chechen separatist leader Zelimkhan Yandarbiyev headed for Moscow on Thursday for talks with Russian leaders on reinforcing a peace deal in the breakaway region.
Yandarbiyev, who flew out of the Ingushetia region bordering Chechnya in southern Russia, was expected to meet Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin and security tsar Alexander Lebed.
Chechnya was also likely to be on the agenda at talks due between Lebed and President Boris Yeltsin at the Moscow hospital where the Kremlin leader is preparing for heart surgery.
Yeltsin, who was not expected to meet Yandarbiyev, was due to make an address on major Russian radio stations on Thursday, his press service said. It gave no details.
The 65-year-old president also held talks with Defence Minister Igor Rodionov on Thursday on issues including financing the cash-strapped armed forces. It was not clear if they discussed Chechnya.

Interfax news agency said Yandarbiyev and his delegation had left the Ingush town of Sleptsovsk at 9 a.m. (0500 GMT). A rebel spokesman said Yandarbiyev expected to meet Chernomyrdin as well as Lebed.

A ceasefire agreed under the August 31 peace deal in Chechnya has held, but the planned withdrawal of Russian troops from the region is proceeding slowly. Prisoner exchanges have also not gone as well as planned.
Critics say the separatist rebels, who want indepednence from Russia, have got away with too much.

Lebed walked out of the lower house of parliament on Wednesday after deputies heckled and jeered him when he addressed them about the agreement, intended to end nearly 21 months of fighting which killed tens of thousands.

Interior Minister Anatoly Kulikov, adding his voice to a chorus of condemnation for the agreement, won thunderous applause when he said Lebed's agreement was a humiliating step towards Russia's disintegration.

Chernomyrdin has previously played go-between with Lebed over Chechnya. But he has given Lebed's deal a lukewarm response and it is not clear what his renewed involvement in the peace process will achieve.
Chernomyrdin, 58, has taken over some of Yeltsin's powers in the run-up to the president's heart bypass operation which is due in the next six to 10 weeks.

Presidential chief-of-staff Anatoly Chubais said on Wednesday that the Kremlin leader was in full control. He said anyone thinking Yeltsin's illness meant it was time to fight for power would be acting prematurely.

Opposition groups were expected to hold rallies around Moscow's television tower on Thursday to mark the 1993 confrontation between the security forces and supporters of hardline parliamentarians Yeltsin accused of blocking reforms.
More than 120 people were killed in the clashes and in subsequent battles around the White House parliament building before Yeltsin defeated his political foes.
